fda.event_page_status: No minutes posted; content current as of 08/06/2026 when checked.
fda.category2_status: Emideltide (DSIP) is listed under 'Bulk drug substances nominated but withdrawn'. Page content current as of 04/22/2026.
fda.category2_text: Compounded drugs containing emideltide may pose risk for immunogenicity for certain routes of administration and may have complexities with regard to peptide-related impurities and API characterization. FDA has not identified safety-related information regarding emideltide for the proposed route of administration. Therefore, the agency lacks sufficient information to know whether the drug would cause harm if administered to humans.

fda.faers_note: All 13 'DELTARAN' reports are from a German brand-name collision (reports for arthritis/pain, i.e. a diclofenac product), not the Russian DSIP preparation; excluded. DSIP/emideltide: zero, matching FDA's search through March 3, 2024.

ndc_directory.note: Bulk-ingredient (API powder) registrations, not FDA approvals. Labelers not named here.

enforcement.reason_for_recall: Lack of Assurance of Sterility: due to concerns with production processes which cannot assure sterility of products intended to be sterile.
enforcement.note: One FDA enforcement record (2020) for a compounded DSIP vial among products recalled for lack of sterility assurance. Firm not named here.

vote.result: 6 yes, 7 no, 1 abstain on both emideltide forms (as transcribed; no official minutes)
vote.group_note: 'new' = the eight members seated in 2026 per the PeptideBase/CSPI rosters. Individual votes are not reproduced on the page.

analysis.note: Jabbit tally. Four of the five positive human sleep reports come from the Basel research group that discovered DSIP (the fifth is an uncontrolled open-label series); the two independent placebo-controlled insomnia studies found little or no benefit. All human dosing was IV; sold products are SC injection or nasal spray.
